fundamental.headline: Mixed business, and expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 16% over the last year, it keeps 28 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, it carries meaningful debt.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying more than usual: its price vs sales is higher than 95% of the last 5 years. It also looks pricier than similar companies once growth is considered.
drivers: Sales growth is speeding up compared with six months ago.
news: No major company news in the last two weeks.
fundamental.take: Average business at a premium price: there are better places to put money right now. This is research, not personal advice.

timing.label: No rush
timing.text: Nothing urgent in the next few weeks.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 18% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 16% last year; 13%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: Not meaningful (the company holds more cash than its debt plus equity, or data is missing); return on shareholders' equity 81% (3 years ago 106%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $1.7B, down 0% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Profit leans on non-operating gains: net income $5.3B vs operating income $632M over the last 12 months (e.g. investment gains or one-offs that may not repeat).

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 13%/yr over 3 years and 14%/yr over 5 years.

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $3.8B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($2.7B buybacks + $1.1B dividends) = 2.1% of the company's market value. Share count down 1.0% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $7.10, up 8% in 90 days (up 6% in the last 30); 16 analysts raised, 2 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $5.77, up 6% in 90 days (up 6% in the last 30); 20 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Semiconductor Process Control 91% of sales, up 29%; PCB And Component Inspection 6% of sales, up 28%; Specialty Semiconductor Process 3% of sales, up 16%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +39% vs a year ago · $4.01 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 39% vs sales 29%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running, but the beats are shrinking (5% → 3%): the bar is getting harder to clear.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 29% from a year ago and speeding up (from 11% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $4 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 77% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 34× last year's profit (higher than 67% of the last 5 years); only 20× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Jan 28; analysts expect EPS of $1.45, up 63% from a year ago. It usually moves about 5% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 8% in 90 days (16 raised, 2 cut lately): forecasts are edging up.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
